reviewedFrom: Intercompany as one ledger with company segments (docs/books-entities.md): a line belongs to the company that owns its account or job; unowned cash, undeposited funds and cards belong to the primary company; each posting adds due-from/due-to legs so every company balances alone, settling what is already owed first. Amounts are integer cents.

company-business.derivation: Start at zero after the closed July. Aug 3 the builder advances 500.00 (land owes 500); Aug 10 it pays the land company's 200.00 survey bill from its operating cash (700); Aug 15 a 120.00 payroll summary for the land crew paid by the builder (820); Aug 20 the land company repays 300.00 (520); the builder's 100.00 insurance is allocated 60/40, 40.00 to the land job (560); Aug 28 a 50.00 land expense paid by the builder fails while its reciprocal leg is written (nothing posts, still 560), then posts once with two intercompany legs on retry, a second retry adding nothing (610). Both companies agree on every date, each balances alone, and a July entry is refused because July is closed.
